L361:     def _failure_text(self, error: Exception) -> str:
L362:         """Caller-facing text for a FAILED task status.
L363: 
L364:         Delegates to the injected ``ErrorMapper``, this package's single
L365:         error-redaction policy, so the task-status surface classifies exactly
L366:         like the JSON-RPC surface instead of collapsing every code to one
L367:         string:
L368:         - internal / unrecognized errors keep the fixed ``"Internal server
L369:           error"`` (srs FR-ERR-004 / FR-ERR-008, locked by the shared
L370:           ``error_mapping.json`` and ``streaming_events.json`` fixtures);
L371:         - ``ACL_DENIED`` carries the fixed ``"Access denied"`` message (srs FR-ERR-003);
L372:         - caller-fixable classes (schema validation, invalid input, unknown
L373:           module) carry their sanitized detail, which srs FR-ERR-002 requires
L374:           precisely so a caller "can correct their input without guessing".
L375:         For those detail-carrying classes the error's ``ai_guidance`` is
L376:         appended when apcore supplied one: it exists to tell an agent what to do
L377:         next, and an A2A caller sees only this status message. It is withheld
L378:         for every other class, where the message is a fixed per-class string
L379:         that must stay fixed.
L380:         The gate is :func:`~apcore_a2a.adapters.errors.carries_caller_detail` —
L381:         the same partition ``ErrorMapper`` itself branches on. Gating on
L382:         ``error.user_fixable`` instead would be a different partition: six
L383:         apcore codes are ``user_fixable=True`` yet fall into the mapper's
L384:         catch-all, so e.g. a ``DEPENDENCY_NOT_FOUND`` failure would send the
L385:         caller ``"Internal server error (module 'x' requires 'y' >= 2.1; ...)"``
L386:         — the deliberately-opaque string extended with dependency-graph detail
L387:         that :func:`~apcore_a2a.adapters.errors.sanitize_message` does not strip
L388:         (it removes only paths and traceback-shaped lines, not module ids,
L389:         versions, env-var names or hostnames). ``user_fixable`` is settable
L390:         per-error by the module author, so any module could widen the fixed
L391:         string further.
L392:         """
L393:         message = str(self._error_mapper.to_jsonrpc_error(error).get("message", ""))
L394:         guidance = getattr(error, "ai_guidance", None)
L395:         disclose = getattr(self._error_mapper, "disclose_refusal_reason", False)
L396:         if carries_caller_detail(error, disclose) and isinstance(guidance, str) and guidance.strip():
L397:             return f"{message} ({sanitize_message(guidance)})"
L398:         return message

L50: class ErrorMapper:
L51:     """Maps apcore exceptions to A2A JSON-RPC error dicts.
L52:     Security note: a governance refusal conveys its *class* and suppresses its
L53:     *detail*; internal errors never expose file paths, caller identity, or stack
L54:     traces to the caller.
L55:     """
L56:     def __init__(self, *, disclose_refusal_reason: bool = False) -> None:
L57:         """Args:
L58:         disclose_refusal_reason: Forward apcore's own message for the three
L59:             governance refusal codes instead of the fixed per-class string
L60:             (srs FR-ERR-011). Off by default. The code never changes with the
L61:             flag — what a refusal *is* does not depend on how much a deployment
L62:             chooses to say about it.
L63:         """
L64:         self._disclose_refusal_reason = disclose_refusal_reason
L65:     @property
L66:     def disclose_refusal_reason(self) -> bool:
L67:         """Whether governance refusals forward apcore's own reason."""
L68:         return self._disclose_refusal_reason
L69: 
L70:     def format(self, error: Exception, context: object = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
L71:         """ErrorFormatter protocol implementation for apcore ErrorFormatterRegistry.
L72: 
L73:         Args:
L74:             error: The error to format.
L75:             context: Optional context (unused, present for protocol compliance).
L76:         Returns:
L77:             Dict with "code" (int) and "message" (str) keys.
L78:         """
L79:         return self.to_jsonrpc_error(error)
L80: 
L81:     def to_jsonrpc_error(self, error: Exception) -> dict[str, Any]:
L82:         """Convert an exception to an A2A JSON-RPC error dict.
L83: 
L84:         Args:
L85:             error: Exception to convert.
L86:         Returns:
L87:             Dict with "code" (int) and "message" (str) keys.
L88:         """
L89:         # Log full detail for server-side diagnosis
L90:         logger.error("A2A error: %s", error, exc_info=True)
L91: 
L92:         # Check for apcore-style errors with a .code attribute
L93:         error_code = getattr(error, "code", None)
L94: 
L95:         if error_code is not None:
L96:             return self._handle_apcore_error(error, error_code)
L97:         # asyncio.TimeoutError
L98:         if isinstance(error, asyncio.TimeoutError):
L99:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Execution timeout"}
L100: 
L101:         # All other exceptions
L102:         return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Internal server error"}
L103: 
L104:     def _handle_apcore_error(self, error: Exception, error_code: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
L105:         """Handle an apcore error with a .code attribute.
L106:         Args:
L107:             error: The apcore exception.
L108:             error_code: The string error code from error.code.
L109: 
L110:         Returns:
L111:             JSON-RPC error dict.
L112:         """
L113:         if error_code == ErrorCodes.MODULE_NOT_FOUND:
L114:             # Extract module ID from message if possible
L115:             message = self._sanitize_message(getattr(error, "message", str(error)))
L116:             return {"code": _CODE_METHOD_NOT_FOUND, "message": message}
L117:         if error_code == ErrorCodes.SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR:
L118:             # apcore raises the one code for output validation too, which the
L119:             # caller can do nothing about — see is_server_side_schema_error.
L120:             if is_server_side_schema_error(getattr(error, "message", str(error))):
L121:                 return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Internal server error"}
L122:             return {"code": _CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "message": _schema_error_message(error)}
L123:         if error_code == ErrorCodes.GENERAL_INVALID_INPUT:
L124:             description = self._sanitize_message(getattr(error, "message", str(error)))
L125:             return {"code": _CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "message": f"Invalid input: {description}"}
L126:         if error_code in _GOVERNANCE_REFUSALS:
L127:             # The A2A spec §13.2 MUST NOT forbids revealing *the existence of a
L128:             # resource*, not the *class* of failure. A fixed "Access denied" /
L129:             # "Approval denied" / "Approval timed out" names no caller, target,
L130:             # approver or rule, so it discloses nothing — a caller that named a
L131:             # skill already held that id — while still telling an agent to stop
L132:             # rather than retry.
L133:             #
L134:             # APPROVAL_PENDING is deliberately absent: it is a resumable pause
L135:             # carrying the approval_id the caller resumes with, handled by the
L136:             # executor before it ever reaches here (srs FR-EXE-002).
L137:             return {
L138:                 "code": _GOVERNANCE_CODES[error_code],
L139:                 "message": self._refusal_message(error, error_code),
L140:             }
L141:         if error_code == ErrorCodes.MODULE_TIMEOUT:
L142:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Execution timeout"}
L143: 
L144:         if error_code == ErrorCodes.EXECUTION_CANCELLED:
L145:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Execution cancelled"}
L146:         if error_code in (
L147:             ErrorCodes.CALL_DEPTH_EXCEEDED,
L148:             ErrorCodes.CIRCULAR_CALL,
L149:             ErrorCodes.CALL_FREQUENCY_EXCEEDED,
L150:         ):
L151:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Safety limit exceeded"}
L152: 
L153:         if error_code in (ErrorCodes.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN, ErrorCodes.TASK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED):
L154:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Service temporarily unavailable"}
L155:         if error_code == ErrorCodes.MODULE_DISABLED:
L156:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Module is currently disabled"}
L157: 
L158:         if error_code in (
L159:             ErrorCodes.CONFIG_NAMESPACE_DUPLICATE,
L160:             ErrorCodes.CONFIG_MOUNT_ERROR,
L161:             ErrorCodes.CONFIG_BIND_ERROR,
L162:         ):
L163:             return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Configuration error"}
L164:         # Unknown apcore error code
L165:         return {"code": _CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "message": "Internal server error"}

L167:     def _refusal_message(self, error: Exception, error_code: str) -> str:

L245: def _schema_error_message(error: Exception) -> str:
L246:     """Preserve canonical JSON Pointers without treating them as file paths."""
L247:     details = getattr(error, "details", None)
L248:     errors = details.get("errors") if isinstance(details, dict) else None
L249:     diagnostics: list[str] = []
L250:     if isinstance(errors, list):
L251:         for entry in errors:
L252:             if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not all(
L253:                 isinstance(entry.get(key), str) for key in ("path", "keyword", "message")
L254:             ):
L255:                 continue
L256:             # Only the structured pointer bypasses filesystem-path redaction.
L257:             path = entry["path"] or "<root>"
L258:             keyword = sanitize_message(entry["keyword"])
L259:             message = sanitize_message(entry["message"])
L260:             diagnostics.append(f"{path} [{keyword}]: {message}")
L261:     if diagnostics:
L262:         return "; ".join(diagnostics)[:500]
L263:     return sanitize_message(getattr(error, "message", str(error)))

L265: def sanitize_message(message: str) -> str:
L266:     """Strip file paths, traceback lines, and truncate to 500 characters.
L267:     Module-level so the task-status surface (``server.executor``) applies exactly
L268:     the same redaction as the JSON-RPC surface.
L269:     """
L270:     # Match Unix absolute paths (single or multi-component) and ~ paths
L271:     message = re.sub(r"~?/[^\s]*", "", message)
L272:     # Strip traceback lines
L273:     message = re.sub(r"(?m)^.*(?:Traceback|File \"|line \d+).*$", "", message)
L274:     # Collapse internal whitespace (kept in sync with the TypeScript binding)
L275:     message = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", message).strip()
L276:     return message[:500]
